ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the input voltage Ui; the upper positive terminal passes through a series resistor R and then reaches the upper node; from this node downward, a Zener diode VZ and a load resistor Ro are respectively connected, both of which are connected to the bottom common negative terminal rail, so VZ and Ro are connected in parallel across the output terminal Uo. Reasoning: When the circuit is regulating normally, the output node voltage is equal to the Zener diode stable voltage Uz=6 V. The voltage across the series resistor R is Ui-Uz=10-6=4 V, so the current through R is 4 V / 0.5 kΩ = 8 mA. The voltage across the load Ro is also 6 V, so the load current is 6 V / 1 kΩ = 6 mA. The series resistor current is divided into the load current and the Zener diode current, therefore IVZ=8 mA-6 mA=2 mA.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image that R feeds a node where VZ and R_o are parallel to the bottom rail. Use the text values U_i=10 V, U_Z=6 V, R=0.5 kΩ, R_o=1 kΩ. Since the circuit works normally, set the node/output voltage to 6 V. Compute current through R, compute load current through R_o, and subtract the load current from the resistor current to get the zener current.
